subject: Vision reset: cross-pillar span alignment & QBR readout planning
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: partners@cloudbridge.io
Date: 2028-04-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Vision reset: cross-pillar span alignment & QBR readout planning

Team —

Over the last two quarters we’ve grown capability areas quickly, and the current span overlap between Platform, Serving Runtime, and Reliability is starting to create drag on decision velocity. Before the QBR readout next week I want to surface a short vision reset and propose a minimal set of boundary clarifications we can land on that preserve focus and minimize disrupting ongoing projects.

Attached: vision-reset-brief-v1.pdf (slide deck) and a working span-mapping-table.xlsx.

High-level ask:
- Review the attached brief by EOD Friday (2028-04-13)
- Flag any risks to active Q2 commitments and add comments to the Drive doc
- We’ll meet Tue 2028-04-16 09:00-10:00 PT for a 1-hr leader alignment session; please bring 2 slides max of proposed role/charter adjustments and impact on OKRs.

Proposed principles (short):
1) Ownership by outcome (who owns latency & throughput SLOs end-to-end)
2) Clear carve-outs for infra vs. product-facing SDKs (reduce coordination cycles)
3) Temporary charters for cross-functional initiatives with a 3-month sunset and explicit handoffs

Example proposals in brief (tl;dr):
- Serving Runtime keeps model execution, kernel selection, and KV cache mechanics; Platform owns runtime orchestration, autoscale policies, and infra pricing telemetry.
- Reliability (SRE) to own incident response, postmortems, and cross-region failover policies — we’ll map dependences in the attached sheet.

I don’t want this to be a big reorg announcement — think of it as clarifying who writes which playbooks so we can move faster. Please reply with availability and any immediate objections.

Thanks —
Neha
VP, Product & Strategy
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: vision-reset-brief-v1.pdf (PDF slide deck, 12 slides)
Attachment: span-mapping-table.xlsx (Excel, working table)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-10T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Vision reset: cross-pillar span alignment & QBR readout planning

Neha —
Thanks for the concise brief. Quick thoughts after a skim of the slides and the table:

- Support the principles. I think the product-facing SDKs callout is critical (we’ve been spending too much time triaging SDK bugs that are actually platform config issues).
- Concern: the current wording assigns "autoscale policies" to Platform. That is operationally tied to runtime behavior during high-concurrency bursts; if Platform owns policy but not the execution knobs, we risk oscillation during incidents. Suggest we define a joint SLA for short-lived autoscale tuning (Platform owns policy + rollout cadence; Serving Runtime owns execution and rollback triggers).
- FYI: I’ve annotated the span-mapping sheet with two examples where handoffs were unclear for the last incident (INF-1983).

I can prepare the two slides for the Tue session and propose the joint SLA language.

—Marissa
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Vision reset: cross-pillar span alignment & QBR readout planning

Neha and all —
Thanks for starting this. A couple concrete items I’ll bring to the Tue session:

- Draft rollout timeline (3 phases):
  * Phase 0 (2 weeks): leader alignment + OKR impact capture
  * Phase 1 (4–6 weeks): pilot boundary clarifications on one critical flow (Model serving path) with a single canary team
  * Phase 2 (quarter): broader rollouts and playbook codification

- Proposed definitions for handoff events (I added definitions in the Drive doc):
  * "SLO ownership switch": how we record and communicate the moment responsibility moves between teams for a given metric
  * "Operational rollback authority": who can roll back policy changes during incidents

- Suggested agenda for Tue (45m alignment + 15m decision capture):
 1) 5m framing (Neha)
 2) 10m review of proposed boundaries (slides)
 3) 15m discuss SLA/joint-ownership examples (Marissa/Karthik)
 4) 10m agree temporary charters and pilots
 5) 10m assign immediate owners and communication plan for QBR readout

Link to draft timeline and the updated span sheet: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-vision-reset (see "timeline-v1" and "span-mapping-table - annotated").

I’ll own the timeline doc and can take point on the pilot plan if we’re aligned.

—Karthik
Head of Platform
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick turn. Short update after reading comments and the annotated sheet:

Decisions for Tue session (we’ll capture in the meeting minutes):
- Proceed with the leader alignment meeting on Tue 2028-04-16 09:00 PT.
- Adopt the joint SLA approach for autoscale policies; Marissa + Karthik to draft wording by Mon 2028-04-15 EOB.
- Pilot scope: Model serving critical path (Phase 1) — Karthik to lead pilot; Mina to co-own operational runbooks.
- Temporary charters: all pilots will have a 3-month sunset; owner is responsible for handoff playbook.

Action items (owners & deadlines):
- Marissa: SLA wording + 2 slides (2028-04-15 17:00 PT)
- Karthik: Pilot runbook outline + timeline (2028-04-15 17:00 PT)
- Mina: Incident examples + SLO handoff template (2028-04-15 17:00 PT)
- Jonas: Draft QBR readout slide that summarizes the ask and the pilot (2028-04-15 17:00 PT)
- Neha: consolidate final leader slide pack + email QBR notes to execs post-meeting (2028-04-16 12:00 PT)

Please confirm if any of the owners cannot make the Mon EOB deadlines; if silent, I’ll assume acceptance and proceed to finalize slides.

Thanks again — good momentum.
Neha
VP, Product & Strategy
Redwood Inference
